title: Zigzag Over the Diagonals

concept.title: Cells on one diagonal share i + j
body: All cells on one anti-diagonal (running from bottom left to top right) have the same sum `i + j`. The diagonals are numbered `s = 0, 1, ..., n + m - 2`. For a given `s` the valid rows `i` run from `max(0, s - m + 1)` to `min(n - 1, s)`, and the column is `s - i`.
Going diagonal by diagonal, and only choosing the direction of each one, is much simpler than steering a pointer around the edges.

statement: Print the elements of a matrix with `n` rows and `m` columns diagonal by diagonal, in a zigzag. Start with the top left cell. The next diagonal contains the cells `(0, 1)` and `(1, 0)` and is read from top to bottom, the one after it is read from bottom to top, and so on, alternating.
inputFormat: The next `n` lines have `m` integers each.
outputFormat: Print the `n * m` elements on one line.
hints: The cells of one diagonal have the same value of `i + j`.
For diagonal `s`, the row `i` goes from `max(0, s - m + 1)` to `min(n - 1, s)`.
Odd diagonals are read with `i` increasing, even diagonals with `i` decreasing.
